title: Three Postdoc Positions
body:
https://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/node/86241

Closing date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 - 12:00 UK

We are currently inviting applications for three Postdoctoral Research Associates to work with Professors Mezei, Schafer-Nameki, and Sparks at the Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford. These are three-year, fixed-term positions, funded by three different research grants from the ERC, UKRI, and STFC. The successful candidate will be expected to be in post by 1 October 2027.
The successful candidates will be part of a research group with responsibility for carrying out research in either 1) many-body quantum chaos and related fields, 2) application of generalized symmetries to many-body quantum systems and quantum information, 3) low-dimensional or twisted holography and its interplay with generalized symmetries.

They will all be expected to conduct research which falls within the remit of this large-scale project and will have the opportunity to do so in several ways including independently, collaboratively with other members of the group at Oxford and/or with other mathematicians internationally.

Please direct informal enquiries to the HR Administrator (email: placeholder@example.org), quoting vacancy reference 189690.

Reference Letters: Applicants are responsible for contacting three referees and ensuring that reference letters are uploaded to the portal by the closing date.

Applications for this vacancy are to be made online. To apply for this vacancy and for further information, including a job description and selection criteria, please click on the link below:

https://my.corehr.com/pls/uoxrecruit/erq_jobspec_details_form.jobspec?p_id=189690

Only applications received before 12.00 noon UK time on Friday 30th November can be considered.

title: Feinberg Postdoctoral Prize Fellowship
body:
The newly established Carl Feinberg Institute for Theoretical Physics (CFITP) at New York University invites applications for the Feinberg Postdoctoral Prize Fellowship, beginning September 1, 2027. This is a three-year Postdoctoral Associate appointment with a competitive salary, an annual research and travel allowance, and full independence in choice of research direction.

About the Institute: CFITP's mission is to advance fundamental research at the intersection of particle theory, condensed matter theory, quantum information, and quantum gravity leveraging computational and AI methods where appropriate.

The Postdoctoral Associates will perform research within the scope of the CFITP. They are expected to pursue a vigorous research program, to engage across the Institute's research areas, and to participate in its seminars, workshops, and visitor program.

Postdoctoral Associates have access to the full resources of the NYU Department of Physics and to the broader New York theoretical physics community. Postdoctoral Associates are eligible for on-campus subsidized housing, subject to availability.

Eligibility: Applicants must hold a Ph.D. or equivalent qualifications in physics, mathematics, or a closely related field by the start date and should have received it no more than five years before September 1, 2027. We seek candidates working in any area within the Institute's scope, including quantum field theory, string theory and quantum gravity, particle phenomenology, strongly correlated and topological phases, nonequilibrium quantum dynamics, quantum information, and the application of computational and machine-learning methods to these problems. Candidates whose work bridges two or more of these areas are especially encouraged to apply.

In compliance with NYC’s Pay Transparency Act, the annual base salary range for this position is $62,500.00-$90,000.00. New York University considers factors such as (but not limited to) the specific grant funding and the terms of the research grant when extending an offer.

This position is based in New York and the selected candidate will be expected to work onsite as of their effective start date.

Application Process
This institution is using Interfolio's Faculty Search to conduct this search. Applicants to this position receive a free Dossier account and can send all application materials, including confidential letters of recommendation, free of charge at https://apply.interfolio.com/195116
